etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English hochepoche, a variation of hochepot, from Old French hochepot, from hocher (“to shake”) + pot (“pot”), of Dutch or German origin. Equivalent to hotch +‎ pot. Compare Dutch hutspot and German Low German Hüttspott (“hodgepodge”).
senses: (collective) A collection containing a variety of miscellaneous things.
(ambitransitive) To move or position in an erratic, disorganized manner.
